heading: Every region in this archive, and whether it fits on a line
lead: The diagram above draws five families. It does not draw everything, and a reader is entitled to ask what happened to the places it leaves out — Bakar, Fiume, Labin, Trieste, Vodnjan. So here is the whole inventory: **every region where this archive has recorded the surname or the family**, with one of six verdicts against it. Nothing is left in the pleasant middle where a reader might assume it belongs to us.
key: The place is a stop or a destination on one of the five, with documents behind it.
Attached to a line on family memory alone. Drawn dotted above, and it stays dotted until something is found.
A real, documented household of the name that this archive cannot yet attach to any of the five. It may be one of them. It is not being counted as one.
Where the family married, was buried or served — the surname is not from here.
The archive names it for context: a jurisdiction, an archive, a publishing city.

groups.name: Carnia and Friuli — the first line's country
rows: A Zuane De Franceschi of Mione on the 1679 headmen's list of the County of Pazin, with his son. The only document that shows the journey at all.
The valley around Mione, and the Gorto cemetery where thirty and more graves of the name still stand.
An archive, not a household — the Friulian material on the family's supposed home country.
«I nostri in origine erano da Bergamo, poi venuti in Carnia, dove avevano castelli» — Carlo, reporting family tradition at second hand. Nothing behind it.

groups.name: Inner Istria — the County of Pazin
rows: The surname enters the baptism book in 1661; ANNO · DOMNI · 1711 is cut over the door; the benefice held on lease 1772–1848.
Joannes Baptista, farmer of house 5, 1787 — the line's earliest dated ancestor. The Eleven are baptised here.
The county itself, and the town Kobler's Giovanni Battista came from about 1740 — Carlo's own great-uncle's branch.
Darovec names these, with Pazin and Žminj, as where the Friulian-Carnian stratum settled. Our house sits inside that ring; no record of the surname in these three is held here.

groups.name: Southern Istria — the fourth line
rows: Anto De Franceschi with children entered in October 1667 and November 1669 — **which turn out to be Svetvinčenat entries, not Pula ones**, the index having given only «Croazia, Austria». The Pula cluster's own documented run begins later; its earliest firmly-placed people are the Vitorio line from about 1720.
The same family across three centuries of registers. Thirty-one people, 1667–2016.
The last address, not the origin — this archive had that the wrong way round until the family's own tree corrected it.

Seventy-eight records, and Carlo's own book names Franceschi among the nobles of Pola «venuti da Capodistria» before the plague of 1631 — which would make them the extinct Koper family and none of the five.

groups.name: Western Istria — the Crete line's country
rows: Marc'Antonio buys the estate in 1720; 1724 cut on the portal, 1732 on the cistern. A lion on the pediment cartouche.
The parish town: the arms on a canvas of 1650 in the parish church, and the family tomb with ironwork dated 1890.
The second western holding, part of the same estate world.

A title rather than a home — nobles of Capodistria from 1802 while living at Seget — and the town where a Venetian war pension out of Crete was ordered drawn in 1730. A separate, extinct Koper family of the name is a candidate parent for Vodnjan and Pola.

The north-west scatter: four entries at Kaštelir, one Gio Batta De Franceschi at Šterna in 1807 — the exact name-form of Carlo's great-great-grandfather, and nothing more than that. Oprtalj's are Franceschini, a different formation.

One hundred and forty-two records from 1666 — the second-largest concentration in the whole sweep, and now the **oldest**: the register runs from **1657**, and between then and 1737 it names **at least twelve distinct fathers** of the surname. Kandler, Doblanović and Brhan all call the town's De Franceschi Carnian, and Brhan finds a **Stanzia De Franceschi** on the 1820 cadastral map. **And the entries this archive had been reading as «Pula 1667» are from this register.** Still not placed — but it is now the first parish this archive will read page by page.
Aloÿsius Defranceschi, 1615 — the earliest the surname is indexed anywhere in Istria, and forty-six years before Moncalvo. One entry, and it belongs to nobody yet.
Carlo was appointed to the court here in 1850 and Camillo took refuge here in the war. Register entries 1790–1853 are unexamined.

groups.name: Kvarner and the Croatian Littoral
rows: Sixty-six indexed entries, the heaviest concentration anywhere. Kobler found **three separate stocks** in the civic registers and refused to join them to one another. One — Valentino, «venuto dalla Carnia», a citizen in 1739 — is almost certainly ours. **The other two are not placed.**

Twelve people, one household across three generations, from before 1772 to a death in 1819: Dominus Giovanni Battista son of Dominus Francesco, styled *Dominus*, a citizen-class family. **Nothing ties them to Gologorica, to Gračišće or to Kobler's Fiume stocks**, and this archive will not join a fourth household to them on two common Christian names. The family's memory that «there were a lot of Defranceschis at Bakar» is right — and older than the newspapers that were first searched for it.
The stonecutter's son comes down to the coast between 1892 and 1894. The line's own town for half a century.
Anton Rudolf baptised at house 22 in 1890, and against the parents' origin the priest writes «Gallignana u Istriji» — the entry that welds the coast to the county.
A station on the first line, not a line of its own: Ivan went home to Senj and is buried there. Nine graves in the town cemetery.
Giambattista, meant for the priesthood, made castellan here after the Seven Years' War and besieged by forty brigands.

Not the surname — the wives. Antonija Prpić baptised at Krivi Put house 136 in 1859; Ruža Hreljac born at Fužine in 1922; and the Karlobag registers carry the deepest ancestry in the archive — Pilipić, Uroda, Gerkacs, Smojver Vukić — back to people born about 1690.

groups.name: Dalmatia — the Venice line
rows: Cittadini originari of the Republic; Marco Antonio secretary of the ducal chancery in the mid-fifteenth century.
Louis I's charter of 8 March 1359; the family at Zadar from the fourteenth century, and Toma the notary from 1722.
Francesco lays the foundations of his house on 18 June 1584 — and D. Nicolò holds a state vineyard at Vrisovec in the gazette of 1840.
Zuane takes the town in 1717 and is paid in ruined land on the Vrljika; the mills run to fourteen wheels.
The parish the mills sit in. Its death registers 1837–59 were swept opening by opening: not one Franceschi in them.
Where the Dalmatian family is today, the particle stripped off by Napoleonic decree.

Given on the family's own map as the birthplace of the Zuane famous in the war against the Turks. No document — and easily confused with the *other* Seget, which is next to Trogir and is not the family's.

groups.name: The eastern Mediterranean
rows: Nicolò castellan of Castel Milopotamo in 1500; the family noble in Venetian Crete. Candia falls in 1669.
Zorzi de Franceschi goes Candia → Zante → Sebenico, drawing a Venetian war pension the Austrians later restored.

groups.name: Where the name went
rows: Germany — Pfullingen, Reutlingen, Metzingen, Neuhausen, Bad Urach
Zdravko, Petar, Ivan and Felix in the labour camps and then the displaced-persons files, 1941–51. Named individuals, dated documents. The hinge of the whole modern family.

A line drawn on a map years ago from Ližnjan to Monheim, with no note, no date and no name. **Corrected in September 2026: the coordinates point at Bavarian Monheim, and the town that matters is Monheim am Rhein.** The German public directory holds exactly one private listing of «Defranceski» in the country — at **Langenfeld, five kilometres away, in the same district**. Living people, so nobody is named. The attachment stays lore; the place is now real.
«Emigré Australie le 8.3.49» on Anton's index card; Zdravko's bronze at Horsham. Fifteen graves.
Johannesburg. Thirteen of the seventeen people on earth who spell it «Defranceski» are here.
Basilio of Gračišće, born 29 September 1909, at Jackson Heights, and his son Dario born at Gallignana in 1937; Giuseppe born Gračišće 1892, dead New York 1940.

Rotilio, eighth of the Eleven, said to have gone with two daughters. **Searched and not found**: no Rotilio of this surname in the Argentine record at all, and the album's one supporting detail — his wife's name — belongs to his sister's marriage. The register has him at Gračišće, marrying, in 1928. CEMLA's arrival index is behind a bot check this archive will not answer.
Two born at Barban in 1924 and 1931, dead at Charleville in 2002 and at Cannes in 2016. The clearest documented exit from the fourth line.
Domme De Franceski, born in Italy 1880, at the Penn Iron Mining Company at Norway, Michigan, with a wife born in Switzerland. Nothing joins him to Istria.
Brazil — Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, São Paulo
The largest cluster of the surname anywhere, and not this family. Veneto and Trentino: the in-law names are Marcato, Busatto, Poletta, Raminelli, Barbiero, Negri, Catteri, Facco.
Italian-speaking Switzerland, over the border from Lombardy. A different stock of the same ordinary patronymic.
Its own lane above. Documented from 1694 in Napoleón Franceschi's history of it, and never in Istria at any point.
Venezuela · Puerto Rico · Trinidad · St Thomas
Where the Corsican family went, written up by its own historian. Not ours, and the page says so.

groups.name: Places the archive names but no family lives in
rows: Nine entries, and Carlo's grandson Carlo the medievalist was born here in 1900. Otherwise a publishing and archive city: the «Archeografo», the «Atti», the Blasonario, and the diocesan archive that holds the 1788 visitation of the Pićan parishes.
On the Atlas because a document put a man of this family in its orbit, not because anyone was from there.
The «Franceschi dalle Rose» origin story, tested and failed: it belongs to the **Donà** dalle Rose, a different Venetian house entirely.

close: So: five lines; **nine places this archive refuses to attach to any of them**; two attached on lore alone; four clusters of the name that are somebody else's; and a handful of towns that are archives and jurisdictions rather than households. The number worth watching is not how many lines there are — it is how long that third column stays nine.
source_reg: Compiled from this archive's own pages, September 2026: the eighteen-town record sweep, the Bakar household reconstruction, Kobler's Fiume registers by way of Carlo's letters, the Gračišće and Moncalvo registers, Puhmajer on Seget, the Imotski monograph, Napoleón Franceschi on Corsica, and Darovec on migration into Istria.
